paper_metadata.title: A quantum spectral method for simulating stochastic processes, with applications to Monte Carlo

experiments.description: Analog quantum simulation of Brownian motion trajectories using truncated Wiener-series coefficients, a data loader for Gaussian amplitudes, and the quantum Fourier/discrete sine transform.

algorithm.variant: Analog Brownian motion simulation via truncated Wiener series + QFT/DST

hyperparameters.Z0: normalization factor for output Brownian bridge state

problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare an analog encoding of a Brownian bridge trajectory |BL⟩ over T time steps from a truncated Fourier/Wiener expansion.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation of the Wiener series to L terms; unary-to-binary conversion; post-measurement permutation invariance used to handle the random shift.

problem_instance.description: Brownian bridge / Brownian motion trajectory simulation on a discretized time grid.

dataset_specification.description: Discrete-time Brownian bridge on T steps; Wiener series truncated to L terms; examples shown with N=1000, T=2048 and N=100, T=2048 in Figure 2.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate Wiener series; prepare Gaussian coefficients; apply discrete sine transform.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical resource/error analysis; example simulation figures; no empirical benchmark protocol reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare truncated Wiener coefficients; load Gaussian amplitudes with a data loader; use binary-to-unary conversion; apply QFT/DST.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Trace out auxiliary register; interpret output as Brownian bridge trajectory.

speedup_claims.factor: polylog(T) vs O(T log T) / O(T)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical FFT-based spectral simulation / writing down the trajectory
speedup_claims.conditions: for T ≫ L and using truncated Wiener series with L = O(1/ϵ)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents theoretical resource analysis and illustrative figures, not an empirical benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(L + polylog(T)) gate complexity; eO(log L + log T) depth
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T log T) for FFT-based spectral simulation; O(T) to write down trajectory

experiments.description: Analog quantum simulation of fractional Brownian motion trajectories for arbitrary Hurst parameter H using power-law-decaying Fourier coefficients.

algorithm.variant: Fractional Brownian motion analog simulation via spectral method

hyperparameters.alpha: H + 0.5 (power-law exponent used in Monte Carlo subroutine)

problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare an analog encoding of fractional Brownian motion trajectories with Fourier coefficients scaling as k^{-H-0.5}.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation to L terms; same data-loading and DST pipeline as Brownian motion.

problem_instance.description: Fractional Brownian motion trajectory simulation for varying Hurst parameters.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic fBM trajectories; illustrative examples shown for H = 0.8 and H = 0.1; Table 1 reports term counts for H = 0.5, 0.65, 0.8 at error levels 10^-2, 10^-3, 10^-4.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use truncated stochastic Fourier series with coefficient decay k^{-H-0.5}.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical error analysis and illustrative simulated trajectories; Table 1 gives required L for selected H and error values.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Truncate the fBM Fourier series; prepare Gaussian coefficients with power-law scaling; apply QFT/DST.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Interpret the output register as the fBM trajectory.

speedup_claims.factor: polylog(T) dependence and sublinear-in-1/ϵ term count for H>1/2
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical spectral simulation and classical Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: for H in (0,1], especially H>1/2; using truncated stochastic Fourier series
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the result theoretically; no empirical runtime comparison is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(L + polylog(T)) gate complexity; L = O(1/ϵ^{1/(2H)})
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T log T) spectral simulation; classical Monte Carlo O(T ϵ^-2)

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo estimation of time averages/inner products over fractional Brownian motion using coherent analog encodings and amplitude estimation.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo with coherent analog encodings for fBM

hyperparameters.Bmax: upper bound on Brownian path norm for the postselected variant
hyperparameters.f: test function encoded by circuit V

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[<f(t)|BH(t)> / ||BH(t)||] or E[<f(t)|BH(t)>] for fractional Brownian motion trajectories.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Amplitude estimation on a prepared coherent analog state; optional norm-based postselection for bounded paths.

problem_instance.description: Expectation estimation over fBM trajectories for a user-specified function f(t), including time averages and inner products.

dataset_specification.description: Fractional Brownian motion trajectories; function f(t) supplied as a quantum state |f> via circuit V.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare coherent analog encoding of fBM; optionally compute and condition on path norm; encode f(t) in amplitude.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical additive-error analysis; no empirical runs reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare coherent analog encoding of fBM and the function state |f>; compute norm if using the bounded-path variant.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Amplitude estimation output interpreted as the desired expectation value.

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic in epsilon over classical Monte Carlo, plus polylog(T) dependence from analog simulation
speedup_claims.conditions: for coherent analog encodings of fBM and functions f prepared by circuit V
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes the result is a black-box speedup; the exact exponent c depends on H and is stated as 3/2 < c < 2 in the narrative.

speedup_claims.factor: incomparable to standard quantum mean estimation
speedup_claims.conditions: because the analog simulator changes the T dependence but has worse epsilon scaling than O(T epsilon^-1)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly says the algorithm is incomparable to standard quantum mean estimation.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: eO(polylog(T) / epsilon^c) with c = 1 + 1/(2H) in the paper's discussion; theorem states eO((L + polylog(T) + G)/(epsilon ||f||)) oracle calls/gates

experiments.description: Quantum spectral simulation of stochastic integrals over Lévy noise using Toeplitz-to-circulant embedding and QFT-based diagonalization.

algorithm.variant: Quantum spectral method for stochastic integrals

hyperparameters.L: number of largest Fourier coefficients retained
hyperparameters.C: ratio of maximum to minimum Fourier coefficients of the Lévy noise
hyperparameters.b: truncated Fourier coefficients of the Lévy noise

problem_formulation.objective_function: Generate amplitude encoding of F(t) = ∫_0^t K(s,t) dμ_s by multiplying the kernel vector by a circulant embedding of the Lévy-noise Toeplitz operator.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Postselection in the diagonal-scaling step; reversal handling after measuring the auxiliary qubit.

problem_instance.description: Stochastic integral against Lévy noise (including Brownian motion as a special case) with kernel K.

dataset_specification.description: Discrete-time kernel vector K over T steps; Lévy noise Fourier coefficients computed from (μ, 0^T).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classically compute Fourier coefficients of Lévy noise and truncate to L terms; prepare amplitude encoding of K; embed Toeplitz matrix into a circulant matrix.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical correctness and success-probability analysis; no empirical benchmark protocol reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute Fourier coefficients of Lévy noise; truncate to L terms; prepare kernel state; build circulant embedding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure auxiliary qubit and, if needed, reverse the output trajectory.

classical_baselines.method_name: classical fourier transform of levy noise and truncation

speedup_claims.conditions: the paper states the overall resources are O(T log T) and the quantum subroutine is O(L log L + log^2 T)
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly says this result is weaker than the fBM case and does not provide coherent simulation for Lévy processes.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(T log T) resources overall; quantum subroutine O(L log L + log^2 T)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T log T) to compute the Fourier transform of the Lévy noise and truncate

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo application to pricing a variance swap when volatility follows fractional Brownian motion.

algorithm.variant: Variance swap pricing via coherent analog encoding of fBM

problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the strike price sigma_strike^2 = E_Q[sigma_realized^2 | F_t0] for a variance swap, where sigma_realized^2 = (A/n) sum_i R_i^2.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Optional postselection on fBM paths with norm in [Bmin, Bmax] to avoid closed-form simplifications.

problem_instance.description: Variance swap pricing under a model with geometric Brownian motion driven by fractional Brownian volatility.
problem_instance.time_steps: n observed prices over horizon T

dataset_specification.description: Model: S_t = exp(∫_0^t sigma_s dB_s + ∫_0^t (r - 1/2 sigma_s^2) ds), with sigma_t = BH_t.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Compute log returns R_i; use projective measurement onto time steps to estimate realized variance.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical pricing procedure; no empirical market dataset or backtest reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare coherent analog encoding of fBM volatility; tag amplitudes for time steps; compute realized variance from log returns.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Interpret amplitude-estimation output as the variance swap strike price.

results.value: n observed prices over horizon T

speedup_claims.factor: polylog(T) dependence and black-box speedup over classical Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: variance swap pricing with volatility modeled as fBM; especially when H > 1/2
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes the variance swap itself has a closed-form solution in the unpostselected setting; postselection is suggested to avoid closed-form simplifications.

speedup_claims.factor: incomparable to standard quantum mean estimation
speedup_claims.conditions: because the analog simulator changes the T dependence but has worse epsilon scaling
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly states the comparison is incomparable.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(polylog(T) epsilon^-c) with 3/2 < c < 2 (paper states c = 1 + 1/(2H) for this application)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T epsilon^-2) classical Monte Carlo; standard quantum mean estimation O(T epsilon^-1)
